sections.h2: What the Boone County Recorder of Deeds does
sections.html:
This office keeps the public record of land transactions in the county and also issues marriage licenses. Deeds, deeds of trust, releases, easements, plats, surveys, restrictions, cemetery deeds, wills, road rights of way and affidavits all end up in its indexes. If you're selling in Columbia, Ashland, Centralia or anywhere else in the county, the closing isn't finished until the deed reaches this office.

The deed and deed of trust index reaches back to 1821, and computerized real estate records start in 1975. Releases and assignments have a separate index. State and federal tax liens are indexed by taxpayer name, with computerized lien records starting in 1985, and marriage records on computer begin in 1973. The office phone is 573-886-4345.

Copies of every deed and deed of trust go to the Assessor, so the recorded document is what updates ownership for the next tax bill.

A standard real estate document costs $26.00 for the first page and $3.00 for each page after that. Pay the amount the Recorder posts, and call 573-886-4345 if a closing agent quotes something different. Statutory authority for recorder fees is RSMo 59.310.

Card users pay a $1.55 fee on transactions up to $66.00 and 2.35 percent on anything larger. Those charges sit on top of the recording fee.

The Recorder keeps an overpayment of up to $10.00. The reason is speed: documents can be recorded in priority order without being bounced for a small shortfall, as long as the payment isn't below the statutory fee. Anything beyond that is receipted and deposited. To get an overpayment back, send a written request that reaches the office within 30 days of recording, and the Recorder then has 30 days to decide. UCC fixture filings are the exception, since overpayments on those are never refunded.

sections.h2: What a deed must include to be recorded
sections.html:
The Recorder's requirements follow the format rules in state law. A document that follows them records as standard. One that doesn't still records, but as a non-standard document, and a $25.00 penalty is added to the normal fee under RSMo 59.310.

  • Title and date of the document on the first page, below a blank 3-inch top margin.
  • Names of every grantor with marital status, plus the grantees, on the first page.
  • Grantee mailing address and the legal description of the land on the first page.
  • Grantor signature, with the name typed or printed under each signature.
  • Notary acknowledgment with signature and seal, stamped in blank space rather than over text.
  • Letter-size paper, margins of at least three-quarters of an inch elsewhere, and type no smaller than 8 point.

A recording certificate is stamped in the top margin when the document is accepted. A rejected document comes back with a written reason. Documents signed before 2002, military separation papers, papers signed abroad, certified copies, documents where a party has died and court-formatted judgments are exempt from the layout rules.

A few document types ask for extra items, and they matter when a seller is paying off a loan or buying out of foreclosure.

  • A release deed must list the book and page of the deed of trust being released. If that deed of trust was recorded before January 1, 1986, the original note, marked paid, has to come along, or an affidavit of lost note from the maker and holder.
  • A trustee's deed after foreclosure must show the book and page of the foreclosed deed of trust, and the original identified note is required when that deed of trust was recorded before 1986.
  • An assignment of deed of trust should list the book and page of the instrument being assigned.
  • Fixture filings under the Uniform Commercial Code stay with the county, while other UCC filings go to the Secretary of State.

The Recorder doesn't draft deeds or answer legal questions. A title company or attorney handles preparation, and the Recorder's office handles filing and retrieval.

sections.h2: Seller checklist before a deed goes to the Recorder
sections.html:
Most recording problems come from small gaps that a closing agent can catch in advance. A few minutes of review saves the $25.00 non-standard charge and avoids a returned document.

  • Confirm every grantor name matches the prior deed and that marital status is stated.
  • Check that the legal description is on page one, or that page one points to the page where it appears.
  • Leave the top three inches clear and keep notary seals out of the margins.
  • Ask whether a lien, such as a state or federal tax lien indexed by taxpayer name, will need a discharge recorded at $7.50.
  • Request a certified or plain copy afterward, at $1.00 per page plus $1.00 for the certification.

The same counter handles marriage licenses, at $53.00, but that has nothing to do with a house sale.

sections.h2: How recording affects the Boone County tax bill
sections.html:
Because the Recorder passes every deed to the Assessor, the date a deed is recorded can decide whose name appears on the next tax bill. A closing on or after October 1 may produce a bill in the seller's name at the old address unless the buyer reports the sale. Ask the title company to confirm the deed was recorded, then tell the Collector or Assessor about the new owner.

Fees collected here go to the County Treasurer, apart from special fees forwarded directly to the state each month. The Recorder also files a monthly fee report with the Auditor and settles up yearly with the County Commission.

sections.h2: Boone County market and deed volume
sections.html:
Boone County has 84,371 housing units for 2025, and owner-occupied homes have a median value of $272,800. Owners live in 57.7 percent of homes, median gross rent is $1,088, and 787 building permits were issued in 2025.

That adds up to a steady flow of filings: sales, refinances, releases after payoffs and new subdivision plats. Columbia, with the University of Missouri, anchors most of that activity, and the separate plat and survey fees reflect the platting that growth brings. A cash sale records the same way as a financed one, minus the new deed of trust.

faqs.q: How much does the Boone County Recorder charge for a standard deed?
faqs.a: $26.00 for the first page and $3.00 for each added page. A non-standard document costs $51.00 for the first page.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed is not in standard format?
faqs.a: It is recorded as non-standard, and a $25.00 penalty is added to the regular fee under RSMo 59.310. Following the margin, signature and notary rules avoids that charge.

faqs.q: Can I get an overpayment refunded?
faqs.a: Only in some cases. The Recorder keeps overpayments up to $10.00, and larger ones can be requested back in writing within 30 days of recording. UCC fixture filing overpayments are not refunded.

faqs.q: Does the Recorder prepare deeds for homeowners?
faqs.a: No. The office files and indexes documents and helps people search records, but legal drafting belongs to an attorney or title company.

faqs.q: How far back do Boone County land records go?
faqs.a: The general index reaches back to 1821, and computerized real estate records begin in 1975. Call 573-886-4345 for help with older books.
